To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the emission estimates for the USCB subregion are in broad agreement with E-PRTR estimates, (2) the uncertainty of the wind is the main source of error on the emission estimates, (3) the uncertainty of XCH4 is negligible, and (4) the uncertainty of our emission estimates is dominated by the wind-related errors.

(1) the CH4 emissions from coal mines in the Upper Silesia region of Poland are estimated to be 6 to 109 kt a−1, (2) the largest uncertainty of the emission estimate is caused by the wind speed and wind direction variability in the atmospheric boundary, and (3) the XCH4 measurements can be used for emission estimates with a precision of 10 % or less, provided that the wind variability is sufficiently well characterized.

the emission estimates for CH4 based on mobile FTS measurements of XCH4 are in broad agreement with E-PRTR data for the USCB, and that wind uncertainty is the largest source of uncertainty on the emission estimates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of CH4 emissions from coal mines and the associated uncertainties using mobile FTS measurements and wind lidar observations.
a new approach to estimate CH4 emissions from coal mines using a mobile FTS, which is a cost-effective and fast alternative to stationary FTSs.
the development, validation, and application of a novel method for quantifying CH4 emissions from coal mines using mobile XCH4 measurements and wind information from wind lidars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emission estimates presented here are accurate within 30 % to 50 % and that the emission estimates are dominated by uncertainties in wind speed and direction.
the emission estimate of 109±33   kt a −1 (1  σ uncertainty) is the best available estimate for the subregion of the Polish side of Upper Silesian Basin.
our emission estimates are in broad agreement with those of the E-PRRT, but the uncertainties are too large for a more detailed comparison.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated a new, promising method for the determination of methane emissions from hard coal mining, which is based on the combination of mobile sun-viewing FTL (Fourier transform lidar) XCH4 measurements with the mass balance method.
the emission estimates for individual ventilation shafts are robust but the uncertainty of emission estimates for larger areas is dominated by uncertainties in the local wind.
mobile FTS measurements of CH4 plumes are a viable method for estimating CH4 emissions from coal mine ventilation shaft exhausts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mobile FTS approach can provide accurate CH4 emissions from coal mines, and it can be used in a cost-efficient and timely manner to monitor and verify emission reductions from individual mines.

the mobile FTS method, when applied to coal mine ventilation shaft plumes, provides reliable and accurate estimates of the CH4 emissions, even though the method relies on only a few transects across the plume and is therefore very cost-effective compared to stationary FTS measurements.
the mobile sun-viewing FTA can be used to quantify methane emissions from individual coal mine ventilation plume exhausts, which are not accessible by stationary instruments.
